00026 /**
00027  * @brief The gadget type (not to be confused with the gadget object type, 
00028  * below) specifies how the gadget value changes in response to user activity.
00029  * The gadget value is reflected through a set of images provided in an image
00030  * button object (see HxImageButtonObj_t).
00031  * 
00032  * By default, gadgets are like command buttons: they trigger a message,
00033  * but do not change value. Toggle gadgets, on the other hand, behave like
00034  * checkboxes, toggling between the values of 0 and 1.
00035  */
00036 typedef enum HxGadgetType_t
00037 {
00038     kGadgetTypeDefault = 0,
00039     kGadgetTypeToggle,
00040 } HxGadgetType_t;
00041 
00042 
00043 /**
00044  * @brief A gadget can contain one or more objects.  The object definition
00045  * includes a type, which can either by a system type (text or image), or a
00046  * user type.  The toolkit draws a system type using the widget Draw callback,
00047  * while the application is responsible for drawing objects that are user
00048  * types.
00049  */
00050 typedef enum HxGadgetObjectType_t
00051 {
00052     kHxGadgetObjImageButton = -3,           /**< image button object type */
00053     kHxGadgetObjText        = -2,           /**< text object type */
00054     kHxGadgetObjImage       = -1,           /**< image object type */
00055 
00056     kHxGadgetObjFirstUser   = 0,            /**< user-defined type start */
00057     kHxGadgetObjLastUser    = 0x7FFFFFFF     /**< user-defined type end */
00058 } HxGadgetObjectType_t;

00061 typedef enum HxGadgetAttribute_t
00062 {
00063     kHxGadgetAttrNone         = 0x00000000,
00064 
00065     /*
00066         Gadget that can handle mouse and keyboard input events.
00067     */
00068     kHxGadgetHandlesInput     = 0x00000001,
00069 
00070     /*
00071         Gadget that can be reached using keyboard navigation.
00072     */
00073     kHxGadgetFocusable        = 0x00000002,
00074     
00075     /*
00076      * If you use this attribute when a gadget is deleted via HxGadgetDelete 
00077      * it will not call DeleteObject on elements of its array of objects.  
00078      * This allows the user to pass images which are cache'd between multiple
00079      * objects and manage the free'ing of those objects on their own.
00080      */
00081     kHxGadgetDoNotFreeObjects = 0x00000004,
00082 
00083     /*
00084      * If you use this attribute, the gadget area will be drawn with a
00085      * standard widget frame.
00086      */
00087     kHxGadgetHasFrame         = 0x00000008,
00088     
00089     /**
00090      * @brief Set the kHxGadgetNoFocusRing attribute if the gadget is
00091      * focusable, but should not have a focus ring drawn around it.  This
00092      * is sometimes desired for gadgets that use a bitmap to represent the
00093      * focused state rather than a focus ring.
00094      */
00095     kHxGadgetNoFocusRing      = 0x00000010,
00096 
00097 
00098     /*
00099      * @brief If you use kHxGadgetNoButtonEffects, button objects within
00100      * the gadget will use the normal state image for each unspecified
00101      * state instead of additionally rendering special effects to depict
00102      * the button object state.
00103      */
00104     kHxGadgetNoButtonEffects  = 0x00000020,
00105 
00106     /* default attributes */
00107     kHxGadgetAttrDefault    = kHxGadgetHandlesInput | kHxGadgetFocusable
00108 
00109 } HxGadgetAttribute_t;

00227 /**
00228  * @brief               Create a gadget control widget
00229  *
00230  * This function creates a new gadget control widget.  The gadget objects
00231  * are copied into the gadget by the toolkit, so the application is not
00232  * required to keep its object array.
00233  *
00234  * Text objects are duplicated completely, with local copies of the string
00235  * and font definition structures stored in the gadget.  Image objects
00236  * have their HxImageDescription_t structures duplicated, but because there is
00237  * no reference counting implemented in the system, you should NOT
00238  * call HxImageDescriptionDelete on the description that you've passed into
00239  * the gadget until you know the gadget has been destroyed.
00240  *
00241  * When using user-defined objects, the application is responsible for
00242  * initializing both p1 and p2 fields within the HxUserObject_t structure,
00243  * and it is responsible for freeing any data that those pointers may point
00244  * to when the gadget is destroyed.  One way to do this is to override
00245  * the destroy callback for the gadget and do your own processing.  To destroy
00246  * any system objects in the gadget, you can save the original destroy callback
00247  * value and call that to destroy any text and image objects in the list.
00248  * 
00249  * The gadget also holds a value setting which is used in conjunction with
00250  * image button objects to choose a set of images drawn in response to mouse
00251  * actions or when the the gadget is disabled. User actions do not change the
00252  * value (except when initialized via HxToggleGadgetNew), but gadget owners
00253  * can register to receive the gadget selected message and call HxGadgetSetValue
00254  * in response.
00255  *
00256  * @param id            IN:     Unique ID for the widget, defined by app,
00257  *                              or kHxWidgetAutoID to auto-generate the ID
00258  * @param pParent       IN:     Pointer to "parent" widget containing gadget
00259  * @param pBounds       IN:     Pointer to bounds of gadget
00260  * @param objectCount   IN:     Count of objects in this gadget
00261  * @param pObjects      IN:     Array of objectCount objects
00262  * @param attr          IN:     Control behavior of the gadget like focusable,
00263  *                              and editable
00264  * @param hGadget       OUT:    Handle to the new gadget; *hGadget is
00265  *                              NULL on failure
00266  *
00267  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.  Returns
00268  *                              HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails,
00269  *                              and sets *hGadget to NULL.
00270  *
00271  **/
00272 /* value remains at 0 unless changed by calling HxGadgetSetValue */
00273 HxResult HxGadgetNew(uint32_t id, HxWidget_t* pParent,
00274                         const HxRectangle_t* pBounds,
00275                         int32_t objectCount, const HxGadgetObject_t* pObjects,
00276                         HxGadgetAttribute_t attr, HxGadget_t** hGadget);
00277
